title: Aug 8 Results + Aug 9 Preview: Sometimes the Breaks Just Don't Fall Your Way
summary: 7-8 on Aug 8 as favorites stumbled—but I've seen these stretches before

content.value:
## August 8: A Familiar Reminder

You cover this game long enough, you learn not to flinch at a 7-8 day. Been there, done that, got the scorecard to prove it. We went 46.7% on Friday's slate—not pretty, but baseball has a way of humbling you when you least expect it. Five of our picks with 63% confidence or higher came up empty. That's the game.

## The Damage Report

The Phillies couldn't handle the Jays at home—66% confidence down the drain. The Cubs, Reds, and Astros all let us down despite solid projections. Sometimes the favorites just don't show up, and sometimes the underdog pitcher finds lightning in a bottle. I've been watching baseball since the '90s, and nights like this? They're just part of the rhythm.

What did work: The Pirates held serve against the Mets, the Brewers took care of business against Minnesota, and the Tigers showed up in San Francisco. Small victories.

## Looking Ahead to August 9

Here's the thing about a rough night—you dust yourself off and get back to work. Tomorrow's slate brings us right back to the scene of one of Friday's crimes: Reds at Nationals. And you know what? We're flipping the script.

content.title: ⭐ Tomorrow's Top Pick - Aug 9
content.sub: 60% win probability vs Reds | Brad Lord on the mound

content.value:
## The Nationals Bounceback

Yesterday the Reds took this matchup. Tomorrow, we're backing Washington at 60%. Brady Singer brings his stuff to the nation's capital for Cincinnati, but Brad Lord gets the nod for the Nationals, and the model likes what it sees at home.

I've covered enough series to know that Game 2 often tells a different story than Game 1. The Nationals have seen Singer's arsenal now. They've got the home crowd. And sometimes—just sometimes—the team that loses on Friday is exactly the team you want on Saturday.

That's baseball. That's August. And that's why we show up every day.

---

*Max has been covering MLB since the days when box scores came in actual boxes. He's seen hot streaks, cold streaks, and everything in between.*
